name: Microsoft Outlook
oneLiner: Unverified multitenant apps can be blocked from consent

review.what: Publisher verification via Partner Center (optional, but affects whether users can consent)
review.wait: A few minutes once your Partner Center account is verified

cost.text: $0: Microsoft doesn't charge for publisher verification and no license is needed

limits.text: Before verification: the consent prompt shows 'Unverified' instead of a publisher name.
Before verification: with risk-based step-up consent on, users in other tenants can't consent to multitenant apps registered after 8 Nov 2020 that ask for more than sign-in and profile.

requirements.text: Register the app in Microsoft Entra ID as at least an Application Developer.
For other organizations, set supported account types to multiple Entra ID tenants, with or without personal Microsoft accounts.
Publisher verification needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (formerly MPN) partner global account ID.
The app must be registered with a work or school account, not a personal Microsoft account, to be publisher verified.
The publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com and must match the Partner Center email domain or a DNS-verified custom domain.
The person verifying needs Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra, and Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center, and must sign in with MFA.

gotchas.text: Delegated Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and Calendars.ReadWrite don't need admin consent, but their application versions do.
Delegated Mail.Read is available for consent in personal Microsoft accounts.
Composio says 'Needs admin approval' errors are a tenant consent setting; a verified publisher helps but doesn't remove admin consent everywhere.
Composio says an admin approving inside the user's OAuth flow may connect the admin's mailbox instead of the user's.
Application (app-only) permissions always need tenant admin consent.
Tenant admins can turn off user consent, which makes admin consent mandatory for every app in that tenant.
Microsoft recommends tenants allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers.
If an admin consents without prompt=consent, the consent only covers the admin's own account.
Client secrets last 24 months at most, and Microsoft recommends under 12 months.
Refresh tokens last 90 days by default, or 24 hours for single-page app redirect URIs.
Multitenant apps must call the /common or /organizations endpoint, not a tenant-specific one.
